court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: District Family Court, Madurai - H.M.O.P.No.835 of 2022
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnised in 1999. Two children were born out of wedlock. The respondent filed a petition for Restitution of Conjugal Rights. The petitioner sought transfer of the case to Family Court, Chennai.

legal_principles.principle: The domicile or citizenship of the opposite party is immaterial in a case like this.
legal_principles.held: In case the marriage was solemnized under Hindu Law marital relationship is governed by the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act. Therefore, Section 19 has to be given a purposeful interpretation.

legal_principles.principle: The residence of the wife determines the question of jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: It is the residence of the wife, which determines the question of jurisdiction, in case the proceeding was initiated at the instance of the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The place of residence of the wife is a relevant factor in considering transfer petitions.
legal_principles.held: Considering the distance and the difficulties faced by the wife, the Supreme Court has allowed the transfer petition.
cited_cases: Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255]
Geeta Heera vs. Harish Chander Heera [(2000) 10 SCC 304]
Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355]

legal_principles.principle: The difficulties faced by the wife are a relevant factor in considering transfer petitions.
legal_principles.held: Considering the difficulties faced by the wife, the Supreme Court has allowed the transfer petition.
cited_cases: Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255]
Geeta Heera vs. Harish Chander Heera [(2000) 10 SCC 304]
Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355]

outcome.final_order: The petition is to be rejected.
